clue.text: Fox foiled by rats in Africa

definitions.text: Fox foiled by rats in Africa

parts.words: Fox foiled by rats in Africa
parts.note: the Desert Fox was the nickname of a German WWII field marshal, beaten in North Africa by the British 7th Armoured Division, the Desert Rats

explanation.surface: A fox is thwarted by rodents somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal picture is a disguise: the fox and the rats are both wartime nicknames from the North African campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The German commander Erwin of that surname was nicknamed the Desert Fox and was defeated by the Desert Rats.

clue.text: College point of view?

definitions.meaning: one of the colleges of Oxford University
a bay window projecting from an upper storey, a vantage point for looking out

explanation.definitionFit: Oxford has a college of this name, and the word also means a projecting upper window, a lookout point for the view.

clue.text: Made light of note on side-slip

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: a slip is a mistake or a slide out of place, so the letters of side are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone played down a memo about a sideways skid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-slip' looks like one word, but 'slip' tells you to rearrange SIDE into ISED, placed after MINIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To make light of something is to play down or belittle it.

clue.text: Some might shun a fellow author in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the run is read backwards
only some of the letters of the words shun a fellow are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A writer withdraws, perhaps shunning a fellow writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes UNAFEL from inside 'shun a fellow', and 'in retirement' reads it backwards. Sheridan Le Fanu was an Irish writer of ghost stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu was a nineteenth-century Irish novelist, author of Carmilla.

clue.text: Cork this sort of capital?

definitions.meaning: cork is light and stays up on water, so it is buoyant
money in circulation rather than fixed assets is described this way in finance

explanation.definitionFit: Cork stays buoyant on water, and capital in circulation rather than tied up in fixed assets has the same name.

clue.text: Appeal in the cause of virtue

definitions.meaning: an exasperated plea or exclamation, like 'please!'
taken literally, done on behalf of what is good

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exasperated exclamation of entreaty, and read literally it means on behalf of what is good.

clue.text: Sort of mine appears to start with the makings of 13

parts.note: to open something is to start it

indicators.note: the makings are the raw materials, so the letters of answer 13 are rebuilt into something new

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a book of the Bible and also turns on stage

explanation.surface: A type of mine seems to begin with what is needed for a theatrical programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the makings of 13' rearranges ACTS, the 13-across answer, into CAST, after OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface mine dug from an open pit rather than through shafts is of this type.

clue.text: Palm wine-divine in trifle !

indicators.note: the word in shows one piece going inside another

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something of little value
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman is found in a dessert laced with palm wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' tempts as the pudding, but it means TOY; DD (Doctor of Divinity) goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddy is the fermented sap of certain palm trees, drunk in South Asia.

clue.text: Mean tooth possibly taken out?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A nasty tooth might have been extracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' suggests a dentist; in the definition it means having gone out, away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been taken out for the evening is away from their house.

clue.text: Could be grand, making one a profit

indicators.note: making is read as forming something new, so the letters of one a profit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand sum could be earned, turning a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds of profit, but a grand is also a type of large piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is one kind of this keyboard instrument, alongside the upright.

clue.text: Points in the signal-man's line?

parts.note: a railway signalman deals with points, but a signaller tapping out Morse sends short marks alongside dashes

explanation.surface: A signalman's railway line has sets of points.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway points are the false trail; the signalling is Morse code, whose short marks are these.
explanation.definitionFit: In Morse code the short signals are written as small points, the partners of dashes.

clue.text: Fiery love bird

parts.note: fiery means burning, ablaze
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A passionate sweetheart is described as a fiery love bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink wading bird with long legs, found in shallow lagoons.

clue.text: Bashful toe-twiddling creature

parts.note: coy means shy, bashful

indicators.note: twiddling means twisting about, so the letters of toe are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shy animal wriggles its toes nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twiddling' rearranges TOE into OTE, after COY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild dog of North America, related to the wolf.

clue.text: Book turns?

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament
turns are short performances in a variety show

explanation.definitionFit: A New Testament book is named for the Apostles' deeds, and variety performers' routines are also called this.

clue.text: Bible translator is the bloke Dr Lea replaced

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a bloke

indicators.note: replaced means put in a new order, so the letters of Dr Lea are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bible translator turns out to be the man who succeeded Dr Lea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' seems to mean someone succeeded Dr Lea, but it rearranges DRLEA into RDALE, after COVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Coverdale produced the first complete printed English Bible in 1535.

clue.text: Refuse to sanction trip for Wild also

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of Wild also fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An official refuses to approve a journey for Wilde as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey, but it is a stumble that rearranges WILDALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to sanction is to reject or not permit something.

clue.text: Could mean protracted rumination, of course!

definitions.text: Could mean protracted rumination, of course!

parts.words: Could mean protracted rumination, of course!
parts.note: the name split in two reads as a long chewing, champing at length, and it is also a racecourse near Paris

explanation.surface: Something could mean a long period of thought, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally', but it points to a racecourse; the name splits as LONG (protracted) and CHAMP (to chew noisily).
explanation.definitionFit: A famous racecourse in the Bois de Boulogne, Paris, home of the Arc de Triomphe race.

clue.text: Girl employed about one hundred in the plant

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: Angela is a girl's name
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A girl worked for about a hundred days in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the plant' suggests a factory job, but 'plant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall aromatic herb whose candied stems decorate cakes.

clue.text: Not what the soldier said, the judge told Sam

definitions.text: Not what the soldier said, the judge told Sam

parts.words: Not what the soldier said, the judge told Sam
parts.note: in Dickens's Pickwick Papers the judge tells Sam Weller that what the soldier said is not admissible in court

explanation.surface: A judge warns a witness named Sam that hearsay from a soldier does not count.
explanation.walkthrough: This turns on a famous line in The Pickwick Papers: 'You must not tell us what the soldier, or any other man, said ... it's not evidence.'
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is ruled inadmissible as proof in court, which is the judge's point to Sam Weller.

clue.text: Want to replan the East End

indicators.note: to replan is to lay out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants to redesign London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' looks like the London district; 'replan' rearranges E (East) with END.
explanation.definitionFit: A want is a need, a lack of something required.

clue.text: Sad news of newspaper chief -found in river?

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
news that someone dies is sad news

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor's death is announced, the body found in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an obituary, but 'Sad news of newspaper chief' is ED DIES, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swirling currents that turn back against the main flow are seen in rivers.

clue.text: Accent may need polishing

definitions.meaning: a regional accent, especially Irish or Scottish
a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations, which needs shining

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a strong regional accent, especially Irish, and also a stout perforated leather shoe that wants shining.

clue.text: Lad Inge employed in forest clearing

indicators.note: employed means put to use, so the letters of Lad Inge are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lad named Inge works in a clearing in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed in' signals that LADINGE rearranged makes the answer together with IN, so take IN out and rearrange LADGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An open space in a wood is called this.

clue.text: Some drinks for the road?

parts.note: one for the road is a last drink, but these cocktails share a name with passenger carriages on motorcycles

explanation.surface: A few last drinks before heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the road' calls up a parting drink; the answer is both a brandy cocktail and a motorbike attachment, literally for the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon shares its name with a passenger car fixed to a motorbike.

clue.text: Recover fish — about two pounds

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two pounds give two of them

explanation.surface: A fish recovers, weighing about two pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately', but it puts RAY around LL.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover strength or health after a setback.

clue.text: Knight had cancelled the festivity

indicators.note: cancelled means struck out, so the word had is removed

parts.note: Galahad is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table

explanation.surface: A knight had called off the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' looks like part of the verb, but it is the letters removed from GALAHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration.

clue.text: Can be pictured as aiming to rebuild island retreat

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the letters of aiming together in a new order
to retreat is to go back, so the island is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: A plan to rebuild an island retreat is easy to imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island retreat' looks like a holiday hideaway; 'retreat' turns ELBA into ABLE, after IMAGIN from 'aiming'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be pictured is conceivable, able to be visualised in the mind.

clue.text: One might look down on this "night music "

definitions.text: One might look down on this "night music

parts.words: One might look down on this "night music
parts.note: a lover's evening song is sung up to a balcony, so the beloved above looks down on it

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a piece of evening music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look down on' suggests scorn, but means looking down from a balcony at a suitor singing below.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening song sung by a lover beneath the beloved's window.

clue.text: Leader of Yankees captured by wandering posse of Indian warriors

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so one piece goes within the other
wandering means roaming about, so the letters of posse are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Yankee chief is caught by a roving posse of warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges POSSE to SEPOS, and 'captured by' puts Y, the first letter of 'Yankees', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepoys were Indian soldiers serving under British command in colonial India.
